scenes.narration: Your phone can find you to within about *five metres*, out under open sky. It does it by listening to *clocks in space*.

data.title: How GPS knows where you are
data.subtitle: It starts with clocks in space.

scenes.narration: More than thirty GPS satellites circle the Earth, about twenty thousand kilometres up. Each carries *atomic clocks*, and broadcasts the exact time and its own position, over and over.

data.label: Altitude of the GPS satellites, compared with the ISS and geostationary orbit.

scenes.narration: Your phone notes when each signal arrives. The signal travels at the *speed of light*, so the delay reveals the distance. From a satellite overhead, about seven hundredths of a second means twenty thousand kilometres.

steps.title: Signal arrives
steps.text: Your phone notes the arrival time

scenes.narration: One distance puts you somewhere on a giant sphere around that satellite. A second distance narrows it down. A third leaves a *single point*. And a fourth satellite corrects the cheap clock inside your phone.

data.heading: Three distances, one point
data.body: Drawn flat for clarity: in space each distance is a sphere. A fourth satellite solves for the receiver's clock error.

scenes.narration: That's why timing is everything. A clock that is off by just one millionth of a second puts you about *three hundred metres* from where you are.

data.label: Position error from a clock that is wrong by one millionth of a second.

scenes.narration: And the satellite clocks do drift, because of *Einstein*. Their speed slows them by about seven microseconds a day. The weaker gravity up there speeds them up by forty five. Overall, they gain *thirty eight microseconds* every day.

items.label: Speed
items.note: Special relativity: moving clocks run slow

items.label: Weaker gravity
items.note: General relativity: higher clocks run fast

scenes.narration: Left alone, that would add roughly *ten kilometres* of error every day. So before launch, engineers set the satellite clocks to tick slightly slow.

data.label: Error that would build up every day without relativity corrections.

scenes.narration: GPS is really a *timing system*. Get the time right, and your position follows.

data.title: Clocks in space. Distance by delay.
